title: unified-rollouts: add canary weight adjustments and immediate rollback on composite metric breaches
author: Priya Raman
description:
Motivation: Improve the safety and flexibility of canary and A/B rollouts by introducing runtime-adjustable canary weight schedules and deterministic immediate rollback when composite rollout health metrics breach configured thresholds. This PR updates the rollout engine to support dynamic weight adjustments, adds a composite-metric-based safety check that can trigger an immediate rollback (bypass grace windows for critical breaches), and wires the observability queries required for the thresholds.

What changed (high level):
- rollout engine: add `WeightScheduler` with linear/ramp/step modes and runtime API to adjust weights during an in-progress rollout.
- safety: add `CompositeHealthChecker` that evaluates a configured set of metrics (latency P95, error-rate, model-quality regression signal) and exposes a bail-out signal to the controller.
- policy: new rollout policy fields: `immediate_abort_on` (composite-metric id + threshold), `weight_ramp` (duration + mode).
- observability: add telemetry queries and dashboard snippets for the composite metric, and a new alert rule used in e2e tests.
- tests: unit tests for scheduling logic, integration tests for immediate rollback path, and an e2e harness update that simulates probe failures.
- docs: rollout policy doc updated with examples and recommended thresholds for latency and regression signals.

Design notes:
- The weight scheduler operates as a deterministic state machine: initial weight, target weight, ramp duration, and mode. At each scheduling tick we compute the next weight and emit a route update event; the controller applies the new weights atomically.
- Immediate rollback is driven by the CompositeHealthChecker which aggregates metric probes using a weighted quorum: the policy can specify metric weights and a quorum threshold. When the composite score exceeds the configured abort_threshold, the controller will transition the rollout to abort immediately and execute the rollback hook.
- To avoid noisy aborts we maintain two guardrails: (1) a short minimum stabilization window before ramping begins (configurable) and (2) an override flag `force_immediate_abort` that can bypass stabilization for critical regression signals (used by the platform SRE during incidents).

Compatibility and safety:
- Backwards compatible with existing rollout specs. New fields are optional. Existing rollouts without `weight_ramp` continue to use the previous instant-swap behavior.
- Added feature gate `unified_rollouts.dynamic_weighting` (off by default) to allow phased rollout. The console will flip the gate during release.
